title: Worst-case P95 power & latency curves + onboarding playbook for A100/H100/L40S/MI300
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Objective: produce hardware-specific "worst-case" performance artifacts (P95 latency and P95 token power consumption curves) for A100, H100, L40S, and MI300 variants and publish an onboarding playbook that operators and model-owners can use to pin versions or request fallbacks.

Why: Existing perf artifacts focus on median/mean behaviour. We are seeing tail events in production (spiky P95 latency and elevated token-power on some hardware flavors) which cause customer incidents and unexpected autoscaler churn. This ticket aims to make worst-case behavior first-class: measurable, reproducible, and prescriptive.

Deliverables:
- Automated extraction pipeline that emits per-model, per-hardware P95 latency and token-power curves (by sequence length and batch size).
- Canonical artifact format and storage location (versioned S3 key + metadata) for publishing into the public profile catalog.
- Onboarding playbook: how to interpret curves, recommended pin/soft-pin heuristics, thermal/thermal-throttle notes, and ops runbooks for rollback on P95 regressions.
- CI gating job that fails model onboarding if new-artifact P95 exceeds baseline by configurable thresholds.

Acceptance criteria:
- Pipeline runs end-to-end for 4 hw skus and produces JSON artifacts and a human-readable PDF summary.
- Playbook reviewed and approved by Product and SRE (comments addressed).
- CI job integrated into model-onboard pipeline (green for reference models, fails on synthetic worst-case regression).
tasks: define metric schema for P95-latency and token-power curves
instrument synthetic tail workloads (vary seq len, batch, sampling params)
implement extractor that aggregates traces and computes per-sku P95 curves
hook CI gating job into model onboarding pipeline
validate on 3 public models (gpt-like, llama-variant, encoder-only)
decisions: store artifacts as compressed JSON + summary PDF under s3://redwood-profiles/worstcase/<model>/<version>/<hw>/
publish P95 at 99% confidence using bootstrap with 1k resamples
soft-pin recommendation uses multiplier over baseline median (e.g., allow P95 <= 2x median)
do not auto-promote a new pin without operator acknowledgement (manual review required)

notes: Trade-offs: computing P95 with bootstrapped confidence is more expensive but reduces noise from rare outliers; we accept longer pipeline time for onboarding artifacts.
We intentionally separate worst-case artifacts from median profiles to avoid contaminating quick-latency routing decisions with tail-aware constraints.
Operator guidance will include thermal/firmware caveats for MI300 and L40S since these show non-linear token-power trends under long sequences.
